intro:
Use it to show where a page sits in a hierarchy, and to give the reader a way back up it: the project a file belongs to, the section a setting lives in, the steps that led to a record. The trail ends at the page that is open, which is a label rather than a link — you cannot navigate to where you already are.

A breadcrumb describes a hierarchy, not a history. When the reader arrived through screens that are not nested, a back link is the honest control. When the trail would be the only way between a set of peers, use tabs or a sidebar instead.

It earns its place on pages reached through several levels, where the title alone does not say where you are. A top-level page has nothing above it to name, so it usually goes without one.

parts.List: The crumb row. It owns the separators — one between every pair of crumbs, none at the ends — and the folding, so you only ever list items.
parts.Item: One crumb, as a list item. Wrap a `Link` or the `Page` in it; a trail is a list of these.
parts.Link: A navigable crumb: an ancestor to go back to. It renders an `<a>`, so `href` and the rest work as they do anywhere, and `render` swaps in your router's own link. A string label truncates to the space available and carries the full text as a `title`.
parts.Page: The trailing crumb, where you are now. Not a link — it carries `aria-current="page"` and the full foreground, so the trail resolves to it.
parts.Separator: The glyph between crumbs, hidden from screen readers. `List` inserts it for you; it is public only for a hand-assembled trail, where it sits beside the items.
parts.Ellipsis: Stands in for the crumbs a folded trail hides. Static by default; give the root an `onEllipsisClick` and it becomes a button for a menu of the hidden steps.

examples.title: Folded middle
examples.description: `maxItems` folds a deep trail into its first crumb, an ellipsis and its last. The ceiling is the point at which folding starts, not a hard limit: the ends always survive, and a fold that would hide only one crumb is skipped because it saves a slot without saving anything useful.

examples.title: A separator of your own
examples.description: `separator` on the root changes the glyph between every pair of crumbs at once — a slash, a dot, a word. The list still owns where it goes, so there is never one left hanging after the current page.

examples.title: A menu of the hidden steps
examples.description: Pass `onEllipsisClick` and the ellipsis becomes a real button. Here it opens a Menu positioned at the button, with the steps the folded trail left out, so a short trail still reaches everything above it.

examples.title: Long labels
examples.description: The row never wraps. A long label truncates to the space it is given instead of pushing the trail onto a second line, and a string label is given its full text as a `title`, so the cut is never silent.

notes:
### Accessibility

The root is a `<nav>` with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`. When a page carries more than one trail — one in the page and one in a dialog — give each its own `aria-label` naming the hierarchy it describes, so the landmarks are told apart. `Breadcrumb.Page` carries `aria-current="page"` and is not a link, and the separators are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader hears the crumbs rather than a run of chevrons. A static ellipsis is announced as "More"; a pressable one is a button named "Show hidden items" unless you pass `label`.

### Collapsing

`maxItems` is a threshold, not a hard ceiling. Once the trail holds more than that, the first `itemsBeforeCollapse` and last `itemsAfterCollapse` crumbs survive (both default to 1) and the middle becomes one ellipsis. A fold that would hide only a single crumb does not happen, because the same number of slots with the crumb kept is more useful; for the same reason a very small `maxItems` still leaves a first and a last. Without `onEllipsisClick` the ellipsis is a marker, never a button that does nothing.

### One line, and long labels

The row does not wrap. `Breadcrumb.Link` and `Breadcrumb.Page` truncate a string label to the width available, and set the full text as the element's `title`; pass your own `title` when the label is not a string. The separators and the ellipsis keep their width, and the labels share what is left, so the trail stays readable as the space narrows rather than folding every crumb to nothing.

### Built on

The parts are drawn with Base UI's `useRender` and `mergeProps`, so `render` can swap the link for a router's own component without losing its props. There is no state and no dependency beyond the package's existing Base UI, Tailwind Variants and shadcn tokens; `Breadcrumb.List` reads the separator and folding rules from the root through context. The underline and the ellipsis background are a short colour transition, and both are still when `prefers-reduced-motion` is on.
